mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals a demand recovery in consumer durables, which boosts cyclicals and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces wage growth and corporate margin pressure, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained UNRATE > 4.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals broad-based supply chain weakness, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained INDPRO contraction relative to its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% while the federal funds rate remains above 4% signals a divergence between inflation and policy rates, which typically precedes a policy easing cycle and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when CPIAUCSL < 2% and FEDFUNDS > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals improving consumer demand, which boosts discretionary sector earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained RSAFS growth above 0.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate and payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a paradoxical labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, which increases labor market slack and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases AND PAYEMS increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE and PAYEMS both increase in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units for four consecutive months signals a sustained housing downturn, which negatively impacts construction and home-related equities and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained HOUST < 1.2 million for four months.
